sentences.text:
Souvik Dolui And Ors vs The State Of West Bengal And Another
on 20 March, 2023
Author: Bibek Chaudhuri

Bench: Bibek Chaudhuri
20.03.2023 Item No.15 Suman Ct.42 Crr 3593 of 2022 Souvik Dolui and Ors.
Vs. The State of West Bengal and another.

Mr. Abhra Mukherjee Mr. Sauradeep Dutta Mr. S. K.
Mondal ..for the petitioners
Marriage of petitioner No.1 was solemnized with the opposite party No.2 in the year 2018.
Unfortunately, there was matrimonial discord and as a result of matrimonial dispute number of cases were filed by the opposite party No.2.
She filed an application under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was amicably settled on 29 th April, 2021.
Subsequently, the parties filed a petition for mutual divorce under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act and the said suit was decreed on 25 th November, 2022.
As full and final settlement of alimony and maintenance the opposite party No.2 received a sum of Rs.11 lakhs from the petitioner.

However, on the basis of a written complaint dated 7th September, 2019 a case under Sections 498A/406 of the Indian Penal Code was registered against the husband and matrimonial relations of the opposite party No.2 who have approached this Court as petitioners for quashing of the said proceedings being G.R. Case No. 1454 of 2019.
The petitioner is directed to serve notice upon the private opposite party under registered speed post with A/D and file affidavit of service within three weeks from the date of this order.
The State of West Bengal be served through the learned Public Prosecutor, High Court, Calcutta.
In the meantime, there shall be stay of all further proceedings in connection with G.R. Case No. 1454 of 2019 for a period of six weeks.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J.)
